segments.t: KorTTY creates encrypted backups of all your settings, connections, credentials, and SSH keys. Use backup and restore to protect your configuration or move it between machines.
KTPH000Encrypted backupsKTPH001 — All backups are encrypted using either password-protected ZIP or GPG encryption

KTPH000Configuration backupKTPH001 — Includes connections, credentials, SSH/GPG keys, trusted interactive SSH host keys, global settings, JobScheduler configuration, snippets, AI chat history, local-model registrations, and knowledge-store source metadata

KTPH000Regenerable local AI data excludedKTPH001 — GGUF weights, native llama.cpp runtimes, signed-catalog cache, temporary sidecar files, and HNSW snapshots are intentionally not copied into the archive
KTPH000Projects directoryKTPH001 — All saved project workspaces are included in the backup
KTPH001Automatic rotationKTPH002 — Old backups are automatically moved to an KTPH000 subdirectory with timestamps
KTPH000Configurable retentionKTPH001 — Set a maximum number of backups to keep (0 = unlimited; oldest backups are deleted automatically)
KTPH000Import/restoreKTPH001 — Restore from previously created backups with optional overwrite control
KTPH000Flexible decryptionKTPH001 — Both password-encrypted ZIP and GPG-encrypted formats are supported for import
Open KTPH003Edit → Create Backup...KTPH004 or press KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010 (Cmd+Shift+B on macOS)
Select a destination directory for the backup file
The backup is created using the encryption method configured in KTPH000Settings → BackupKTPH001
KorTTY names the current backup KTPH000 in the target directory. If a backup already exists there, it is automatically rotated into an KTPH001 subdirectory with a timestamp appended (e.g., KTPH002).
All saved SSH connections and groups
Key references with encrypted passphrases, plus the copied key files in KTPH000
KTPH000, shared by Terminal, SFTP, and the Mosh SSH bootstrap; the transient KTPH001 companion is not included
GPG public keys for backup encryption
Global application settings, terminal configurations, themes, and AI profiles
All scheduled jobs, host-key pins, and encrypted sudo passwords
Code snippets and script templates with metadata
Saved AI conversation histories and profiles
Local GGUF registrations and typed launch settings, Text/Coding roles, preferred runtime backend/update policy, and encrypted Hugging Face token
Store metadata and source paths, filters, sync modes, and embedding configuration; not the HNSW vectors
Choose or create a credential to use as the encryption password

Password-protected backups are encrypted with AES-256 (via the zip4j library); the credential's password encrypts all files in the archive. Backups created by older korTTY versions used legacy ZIP encryption and can still be imported — the decryption method is read from the archive itself. Note that AES-encrypted ZIPs need an AES-capable tool (7-Zip, WinZip, KTPH000 6+) if you ever extract one outside korTTY.
Choose a GPG key from KTPH000Manage GPG Keys...KTPH001

GPG backups encrypt the backup file using the public key of your selected GPG key. KorTTY creates a temporary ZIP first, then encrypts it with KTPH000 and stores the KTPH001 file. The temporary ZIP is securely deleted after encryption.
If you don't have GPG keys set up yet, use KTPH000Management → Manage GPG Keys...KTPH001 to import keys from your system keyring or add them manually.
Select a backup file (KTPH000 or KTPH001)
If the backup is password-protected, enter the password when prompted
Choose whether to KTPH000Overwrite Existing FilesKTPH001:
KTPH000CheckedKTPH001 — Backup files will replace any existing files in your configuration
KTPH000UncheckedKTPH001 — Existing files are skipped; only missing files are imported
KTPH000Restart the applicationKTPH001 for all changes to take effect

Importing a backup with KTPH000OverwriteKTPH001 enabled will replace your current settings, connections, and credentials. If you are unsure, uncheck this option to merge the backup without overwriting.
Both KTPH000 and KTPH001 backups contain the same files:
KTPH000 — All SSH connections and groups
KTPH000 — Stored credentials (still encrypted with your master password)
KTPH000 — SSH key references and encrypted passphrases

KTPH000 — Copied SSH key files (only keys you placed there via KTPH001Copy to User DirectoryKTPH002; keys referenced in their original locations are not collected). Restored key files get owner-only permissions, and an import merges — it never deletes or, without KTPH003OverwriteKTPH004, replaces keys already present
KTPH000 — Trusted public host keys for interactive Terminal, SFTP, and Mosh bootstrap connections (KTPH001 is intentionally excluded)
KTPH000 — Application settings, themes, AI profiles, terminal defaults
KTPH000 — JobScheduler jobs, host-key pins, encrypted sudo passwords
KTPH000 — Hash of your master password (for verification on import)
KTPH000 — Local GGUF registrations and runtime settings (model weights are not included)
KTPH000 — Knowledge-store and source configuration (vector snapshots are not included)
KTPH000 — All saved project workspace files (KTPH001)
All passwords and credentials inside the backup remain encrypted with your master password. When you import a backup, you must unlock the master password for KorTTY to decrypt the credentials.
Rebuild local AI assets after a restore

The backup excludes KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, and local KTPH004 snapshots. After moving to another computer, restore or download the GGUF files and a compatible runtime, reconnect any external model/source paths, then run KTPH005Update nowKTPH006 in each knowledge store to regenerate its index. The signed catalog cache refreshes automatically or falls back to the bootstrap. Original source documents and external Qdrant data are not part of a korTTY configuration backup.
When you create a new backup in a directory that already contains one, KorTTY:
Creates the new backup as KTPH000
Moves the existing backup to KTPH000
If the number of old backups exceeds KTPH000Maximum BackupsKTPH001, deletes the oldest ones

To keep unlimited old backups, set KTPH002Maximum BackupsKTPH003 to KTPH000 in KTPH004Settings → BackupKTPH005. To keep only the current backup, set KTPH006Maximum BackupsKTPH007 to KTPH001 (old backups are still rotated but then immediately deleted).
On machine A, open KTPH000Edit → Create Backup...KTPH001 and save to a USB drive or cloud storage
Copy KTPH000 (or KTPH001) to machine B
On machine B, open KTPH000Edit → Import Backup...KTPH001
Select the backup file from step 2
Enter the backup password if prompted
Leave KTPH000OverwriteKTPH001 unchecked unless you want to replace existing connections

All backed-up connections, settings, snippets, saved chats, interactive host-key trust decisions, model registrations, and knowledge-source definitions will be available on machine B. Restored host keys are still matched by normalized host name and port, so a changed key remains blocked after migration. Local model weights, runtime packages, source documents, and HNSW vectors must be restored or regenerated separately.
Verify the file path is correct and the file exists. Check the directory permissions.
Password-protected backups need the correct password. Verify you are entering the credential password (from KTPH000Settings → BackupKTPH001), not your master password.
The GPG key used for encryption is missing. Use KTPH000Management → Manage GPG Keys...KTPH001 to import or add the key, then try again.
KTPH000"No password selected for backup encryption" or "No GPG key selected"KTPH001
Configure a password credential or GPG key in KTPH000Settings → BackupKTPH001 before creating a backup.
KTPH000Import succeeded but changes did not take effectKTPH001
Restart KorTTY for imported settings to become active. If you imported credentials, you may also need to unlock the master password after restart.
KTPH000Backup file is larger than expectedKTPH001
Large backups can occur if you have many saved AI chats or a large projects directory. GGUF weights, llama.cpp runtime packages, and HNSW snapshots are excluded and cannot be the cause.
